# A test BSan cannot finish is sized for it, not skipped

Status: `open`, on crustify's `libgit2-crustify/evolution/bsan-sized-tests` at `6336c30`,
awaiting review.

## Signal

Review findings and gate failures that recur across modules: a rule the how-to skills lack.

## Evidence

- `wave-225/batch-1/run-1` (`src/util/strnlen.h`'s module pass): on the wave tip
  `7ef895eb2` BSan's `unit_pub` and `equiv` binaries timed out at 5400 s, each on one of the
  module's tests (`every_nul_position_in_every_bound`, `every_nul_position_matches_the_c`),
  every other test of both binaries having passed. Translation batches run BSan only on the
  tests they expect to trigger it, so the module end was the first BSan run of either.
  BorrowSanitizer's cost grows with a buffer's borrow history
  (`crustify/evolution/bsan-borrow-history-grows`).
- Four `src/libgit2/indexer.c` tests that never finish under BSan are skipped by exact name
  at every module end since `failalloc.c`'s integration, "until the indexer module sizes
  them for BSan" (dashboard Notes), so BSan checks none of their paths.
- `ub_safe`'s `util::alloc::resized_runs_cross_threads` takes about 35 of `ub_safe`'s 39
  minutes under BSan, with "no `cfg(bsan)` sampling" (dashboard Notes, `alloc.c`'s wave 177
  module pass), and `alloc.rs` already ignores one test under `cfg(bsan)`.

`testing-gates` gives BSan its runs and its `timeout`, but says nothing of a test that cannot
finish within it, so each module end chose by hand between a skip, an ignore and nothing.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, after its BSan runs.

## Change

> A test that BSan cannot finish within that `timeout` holds its whole binary past it, so the
> gate cannot pass. Such a test is sized for BSan rather than skipped: in the configuration
> BSan's build sets, it runs fewer inputs, chosen to keep reaching every path it checks, while
> every other build runs it whole. A skip by exact name is kept for a test that no smaller
> input lets finish, and names the module whose batch is to size it.

The record's entry is in the change. It does not weaken a check: a test sized so runs under
BSan where a skip ran nothing, and runs whole everywhere else. A reviewer should still weigh
that a sized test checks fewer inputs under BSan than a test that could run whole would.

## Validation

The run that exposed it, under the change: `wave-225/batch-1` sized the two tests
(a buffer per word offset, and bounds up to 24 bytes under `cfg(bsan)`, past the 16 at which
core's `memchr` scans by words), and each passes alone under BSan in 5.3 s (`unit_pub`) and
4.2 s (`equiv`), where it ran past 5400 s before; plain and the other sanitizers still
sweep to 70 bytes.
EOF

content.content:
# API stability per C item

`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.

## 1. Input

```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```

`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.

Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path.

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
because this document does not record that crate's re-exports.

Every type in a signature is rendered by its canonical path, never by what the
source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.

A record's `paths` lists every public path the item is reached by, from the
crate root through public modules and `pub use`, globs included. An associated
item's are its owner's paths with its name appended.

## 4. Signatures

Each stand-in's `sig` is normalised text by kind:

- **functions and methods**: `decl` holds `const`, `async`, `unsafe`, the ABI,
  generics, the receiver (`self`, `&self`, `&'a mut self`, `self: Box<Self>`),
  the parameter types and return type, and where-clauses. A method also has
  the `impl` header it is declared in, generics and trait included, and a
  trait's method has `default`, whether it has a body. Parameter names are
  left out.
- **structs, enums and unions**: `decl` holds the generics, the shape (`;`,
  `(n)`, `{}`) and `#[non_exhaustive]`. `fields` maps each public field to its
  type, and `variants` each variant to its shape and discriminant.
  `stripped` says whether rustdoc hid private fields or variants. `impls` maps
  the header of every trait impl rustdoc records for the type to its items
  (those it defines and the trait's provided ones it inherits) and its
  associated types and constants; the auto-trait impls rustdoc synthesises
  (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe`, `RefUnwindSafe`, and `Freeze` and
  `UnsafeUnpin` where the nightly records them), negative ones as `!Send`, are
  included, and blanket impls are not, since they follow from the type's other
  impls. `members` holds the items of its inherent impls that stand in for no
  C item, each with its impl header.
- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.

A trait impl's methods are recorded by name only: their signatures are the

shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.

## 2. C items and their stand-ins

A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.

What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:

- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path.

## 3. Locators and paths

Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:

| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |

Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.

A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
because this document does not record that crate's re-exports.

Every type in a signature is rendered by its canonical path, never by what the
source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.

A record's `paths` lists every public path the item is reached by, from the
crate root through public modules and `pub use`, globs included. An associated
item's are its owner's paths with its name appended.

## 4. Signatures

Each stand-in's `sig` is normalised text by kind:

- **functions and methods**: `decl` holds `const`, `async`, `unsafe`, the ABI,
  generics, the receiver (`self`, `&self`, `&'a mut self`, `self: Box<Self>`),
  the parameter types and return type, and where-clauses. A method also has
  the `impl` header it is declared in, generics and trait included, and a
  trait's method has `default`, whether it has a body. Parameter names are
  left out.
- **structs, enums and unions**: `decl` holds the generics, the shape (`;`,
  `(n)`, `{}`) and `#[non_exhaustive]`. `fields` maps each public field to its
  type, and `variants` each variant to its shape and discriminant.
  `stripped` says whether rustdoc hid private fields or variants. `impls` maps
  the header of every trait impl rustdoc records for the type to its items
  (those it defines and the trait's provided ones it inherits) and its
  associated types and constants; the auto-trait impls rustdoc synthesises
  (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe`, `RefUnwindSafe`, and `Freeze` and
  `UnsafeUnpin` where the nightly records them), negative ones as `!Send`, are
  included, and blanket impls are not, since they follow from the type's other
  impls. `members` holds the items of its inherent impls that stand in for no
  C item, each with its impl header.
- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.

### `libgit2/src/util/strnlen.h` wave 225 batch 1: module pass

The module pass, and the module's only review, over batch 0's three paths, for every objective
with `fix`. It files no finding. `strnlen` is `p_strnlen`'s length for every input: the slice
is the pointer and its bound, and `CStr::from_bytes_until_nul` is core's `memchr`, a byte loop
below 16 bytes and word-wise above, as the docs say. It is `const`, safe and anchored
`Replaces` `mac::p_strnlen` with its alias, and no Rust in the crate counts a bounded length by
hand. The equivalence tests reach C's expansion through `git__strndup`, which `StrFree::dup_prefix`
calls on its own copy of the bytes. No C test references the macro, and the ownership store
holds nothing on it. Porting the macro once is sound under `porting-symbols`' Macros section:
the body computes on its arguments alone, both branches give the same length, and libc's
`strnlen` takes its `std` route. The pass adds that evidence to
`crustify/evolution/config-branches-of-one-result`, which stays open.

Gates ran on `end-gates` snapshots under the worktree's `crustify/tmp/`, at 48 jobs, the four
`indexer.c` BSan skips checked against each binary's `--list`. On the wave tip `7ef895eb2`:
plain passes the whole workspace (`lib` 840, `equiv` 528, `ub_safe` 762, `ub_unsafe` 120,
`unit_pub` 67, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 72 and 378). ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it too, except
the known `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest. Miri passes every binary
(`lib` 392, `ub_safe` 194, `equiv` 38, `unit_pub` 32, `ub_unsafe` 19 passed, the rest marked).
BSan passes `lib` 833, `ub_safe` 757, `ub_unsafe` 120 and `hidden_symbols`, but times out at
5400 s on `unit_pub` and `equiv`, each on one of this module's sweeps,
`every_nul_position_in_every_bound` and `every_nul_position_matches_the_c`, every other test of
both having passed. Alone, the `unit_pub` sweep kept one core busy as its memory grew about
8 MB/s: BorrowSanitizer's cost per access to one buffer grows with its borrow history (its
second word offset took 420 s against the first's 90 s, flat at 103 s with a buffer per offset;
`crustify/evolution/bsan-borrow-history-grows`). The fix, `095f69596`, gives each offset its
own buffer, and under `cfg(bsan)` sweeps bounds up to 24 bytes, past `memchr`'s 16. Every other
build sweeps to 70. On `095f69596` plain, ASan+UBSan, TSan and Miri give the tip's results,
and BSan passes `unit_pub` (67, 71 s) and `equiv` (519, 8 ignored under BSan as before, the
indexer skip, 3246 s). The diff touches those two binaries' test files alone, so BSan's other

content.text:
I found nothing wrong in the `strnlen.h` port, but the module-end BorrowSanitizer gate failed on its tests. Two of the module's tests never finished under BSan, so I resized them for BSan only. The work is landed on `refs/heads/crustify/waves/wave-225`, now at `330e804d6`.

**Review (every objective, `fix` on): no findings.** `strnlen` gives the same length as C's `p_strnlen` for every input, and core's `memchr` does scan the way its docs say. The anchor, alias, home and `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` all follow the conventions. The equivalence tests do reach C's `strnlen`, through `git__strndup`, on their own copy of the bytes. Nothing else in the crate counts a bounded length by hand, and no C test uses the macro.

**The macro ported once.** This is sound under `porting-symbols`' Macros section. The body depends only on its arguments, both header branches give the same length, and libc's `strnlen` is reached through the standard library. Read literally, the shim exception for build-dependent macros is ambiguous here for two reasons:
- what picks the branch is the target platform, which Rust can see;
- a shim would turn the port back into a binding.

I added that reading to `config-branches-of-one-result`, which stays open.

**Gates on the wave tip `7ef895eb2`:**
- **Plain:** the whole workspace passes.
- **ASan/UBSan and TSan:** pass except the two known failures, the `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest.
- **Miri:** every test binary passes.
- **BSan:** `lib`, `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `hidden_symbols` pass. `unit_pub` and `equiv` timed out at 5400 s, each stuck on one of this module's two exhaustive tests; every other test in both binaries had passed.

**Cause and fix (`095f69596`).** BorrowSanitizer gets slower each time the same buffer is reused: the second word offset took 420 s against the first's 90 s, and stayed flat at about 103 s with a fresh buffer per offset. Each test now uses its own buffer per offset, and under `cfg(bsan)` stops at 24-byte bounds, which is past the 16 bytes where `memchr` switches to word-wise scanning. All other builds still go to 70 bytes. Alone under BSan the tests now take 5.3 s and 4.2 s. I filed no report, because a gate timeout isn't a defect in the reviewed code.

**Gates rerun on the landed tree:** plain, ASan/UBSan, TSan and Miri give the tip's results. BSan passes `unit_pub` (67) and `equiv` (519, plus 8 tests it already ignored and the one indexer test skipped by name). The other four BSan binaries keep the tip's results, because the diff touches only these two binaries' test files.

**Rebase:** the wave branch hadn't moved, so the rebase changed nothing and no gate needed rerunning. The landing lock was held by a process tied to my CLI (pid 161881) and released after the push.

**Records:**
- The ffimap scan is identical to batch 0's except +2 test lines. `mac::p_strnlen` and every unattributed module are `kept` in the API measurement.
- I filled the Module passes rows and the review rows in the Symbols tests, safety audit and API stability tables, plus a Notes entry. The usage cells are left for you.
- I didn't remeasure coverage, since only the BSan build runs the tests differently; those cells stand as batch 0 measured them. I recorded the tests row's coverage change as not measured (`—`).
- The run dir's `task.json` and `task.md` are committed.

**Proposals:**
- **`bsan-sized-tests`:** a change I made to the `testing-gates` skill, on Crustify branch `libgit2-crustify/evolution/bsan-sized-tests` at `6336c30`, with its record entry. It says a test BSan can't finish is run on fewer inputs under BSan rather than skipped. The evidence is this run, the four skipped indexer tests, and 11 existing tests ignored whole under BSan only for their cost. It needs a review run before it lands. I don't think it weakens a check, but the proposal asks the reviewer to weigh that a resized test checks fewer inputs under BSan.
- **`bsan-borrow-history-grows`:** the BorrowSanitizer slowdown, with a dependency-free reproducer for you to report upstream if you choose.
